**GUAM POWER AUTHORITY’S REPLY**

**OPPOSITION TO ITS MOTION FOR** 
**CONFIRMATION OF SUBSTANTIAL** 
**INTEREEST**

Agency, Guam Power Authority (“GPA”) hereby submits its Reply to Appellant’s 
(“Dooik”) November 17, 2023, Opposition and Appellant’s November 15, 2023 Protest to GPA’s 
Motion for Confirmation of Substantial Interest.

Dooik’s protest denies the people of Guam the ability to be relieved from loadshedding at 
an earlier pace as GPA’s Multi-Step Bid No. GPA-023-23 absolutely addresses a substantial 
interest to the Territory.  Following the aftermath of Typhoon Mawar and the damage caused to 
GPA’s generating units and the under-construction Ukudu Plant it is abundantly clear that GPA
has demonstrated an imminent need for additional power generation as “all existing GPA 
generating units are critical in order to serve customer loads.” (Decl. of John M. Benavente at 
Exhibit A-002). The Yigo Diesel units at issue in Multi-Step Bid No. GPA-023-23 have the ability

to generate over 40MW (megawatt ) of power but today only produce 9MW. (Decl. of John M.<sup>1</sup> 
Benavente at Exhibit A-002 and **Exhibit A-002** attached herein). On any day Guam’s ratepayers 
and the community-at-large suffer when Guam’s peak demand exceeds GPA’s load or generation 
capacity and GPA’s rotating outage schedules take effect.<sup>2</sup> The outages disturb the communityat-large, the Territory, and local and federal government residents and agencies who all rely on 
the use of GPA’s electric power. (Decl. of John M. Benavente at Exhibit A-002, stating, *“GPA is 
the sole provider for electrical services on Guam to residential, commercial, GovGuam and 
military customers”).* As a result, outages have affected Guam’s economy, Guam’s health care, 
individual personal welfare, and public safety. And, the Territory has collectively responded and 
echoed the need to support GPA’s role and its capacity shortfalls; all to protect the Territory’s and 
the government’s substantial interests. (Decl. of Jennifer G. Sablan at Exhibit A-001-002 
(illustrating the partnership sought from Guam’s large load customers to help reduce load through 
GPA’s interruptible load program)) <sup>3</sup>; (Decl. of Beatrice P. Limtiaco at Exhibits, A, B, and C 
(confirming the request and response from the Guam Legislature by the introduction of Bill No. 
201-37 to provide expedited maintenance, operation, and overhaul, of GPA’s diesel generators)).
The Guam’s Public Utilities Commission wrote in support of Bill No. 201-37 indicating that
“Guam is amid an electric power emergency” urging members of the Guam Legislature to “allow 
GPA to procure vendors to maintain, operate, and overhaul its diesel generators” which included
GPA’s 40MW Yigo Diesels. *See* **Exhibit B-002.** The Guam Police Department has also responded 
to the public safety issues outages have caused and now assigns officers to traffic lights where

upon its 50,000 plus ratepayers to “Beat the peak” as the struggle and substantial interests affecting 
the Territory are apparent.

On November 22, 2023 GPA’s General Manager (“GM”) presented the Guam CCU with 
the generation capacity projection for December 2023. (See **Exhibit A-002).** The generation 
capacity lists all GPA’s generating units and the unit or volume of electricity that each generating 
unit can produce. As of December 2023, the Yigo Diesel units now produce 9 MW of power when 
over 40 MW can be obtained. On record, and during the November 22, 2023 CCU GPA work
session the GPA GM stated that the Yigo Diesel units could immediately provide up to an 
additional “25 MW of power” if maintenance and overhauls could be performed to repair and 
rehabilitate the units.<sup>4</sup> This would bring the Yigo Diesels to a total of 33 MW which is nearly the 
equivalent to the amount of power produced by Cabras 2 (a baseload unit) now generating 35 MW 
of power. (See **Exhibit A-002).** Therefore, it is clear that the Yigo Diesel units have a substantial 
and clear effect on the available power generated and transmitted to Guam’s public. And, each 
day any of Guam’s units can be taken offline due to needed emergency repairs. “At times the
operating capacity can drop to 221.4 MW. The 221.4 MW is far below customer demand<sup>5</sup> which 
results in rotating load shedding when necessary.” (Decl. of John M. Benavente at Exhibit A-002).
This operating capacity is reliant and contingent on GPA’s ability to produce and generate power;
so, each time a baseload generator fails or is taken offline, the generation available to ratepayers 
and the Territory is affected.

*<sup>4</sup>See* https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h1nwHwl0ndU.

<sup>5</sup>Customer Peak Demand is not a fixed number. The number increases and decreases as 
customers use more and less power.

A plain reading of 5 G.C.A. §5425 (g) illustrates that the statute only requires a showing 
that the award is necessary to protect “substantial interests” of Guam. The people of Guam and 
the government as a whole have a substantial interest to lift the stay in GPA-023-23 to avoid 
further loadshedding. Approvals are still required before GPA may award the contract; but any 
further delay of the contract, whether by days, weeks, months or more, will affect GPA’s ability 
to increase its generating load to increase needed capacity immediately. And, Guam’s
procurements statutes may not deprive Dooik of a meaningful review since the procurement rules
provide remedies for any contracts awarded improperly or in violation of the procurement rules.
*See* 5 G.C.A. Chapter 5, Article 9.

Statutory approvals by the Attorney General have been sought and remain under 
consideration. GPA is hopeful the elected Attorney General will respond soon and concur with 
its position that a substantial interest exists to allow the OPA to grant GPA’s motion and lift the 
stay. (See **Exhibit D and E** for requests made to the OAG).

Respectfully submitted this 22<sup>nd</sup> day of November, 2023.

SUBJECT: Testimony of Chairman Jeffrey C. Johnson, Guam Public Utilities Commission, on Bill No. 201-37(COR)

Dear Chairperson Parkinson:

## INTRODUCTION

The Guam Public Utilities Commission ["PUC"] appreciates the opportunity to comment on proposed Bill No. 201-37 (COR). The PUC fully supports the Bill.

Guam is amid an electric power emergency. There is currently insufficient load capacity to consistently meet the required demand. This situation has resulted in on-going load-shedding. This Bill is a good first step in providing solutions for temporary power generation and repair of existing diesel generators until the Ukudo Power Plant is commissioned (hopefully in January 2026).

## THIS BILL SHOULD HELP IN ENABLING GPA TO MITIGATE THE PROBLEM OF ONGOING ISLAND-WIDE LOAD SHEDDING

---

The Bill would waive certain requirements in the Procurement Law to allow GPA to procure vendors to maintain, operate, and overhaul diesel generators, “specifically described as 40MW Yigo diesels, 24MW Tenjo Diesels, 6MW MDI/Pulantat Diesels, and 6MW Talofofo Diesels.”

The Bill would allow GPA to select vendors without complying with the ordinary Source Selection and Contract Formation procedures in the Procurement Law. Provisions allowing protests to stay procurements until resolution would also be waived.

## PUC SUGGESTS CERTAIN AMENDMENTS TO THE BILL

There is presently pending before the PUC an application of GPA to procure 40MW of Temporary Power. GPA should also be allowed to seek 40MW of temporary power under the provisions of this Bill. This addition fits nicely into the Bill, as Section 1 already mentions “temporary power generation” as part of the “responsible solutions.”

The Bill Name would be amended to read: “AN ACT TO ADD NEW §8113.15 TO CHAPTER 8 OF TITLE 12 OF THE GUAM CODE ANNOTATED, RELATIVE TO PROVIDING TEMPORARY POWER AND MAINTENANCE, OPERATION AND OVERHAUL OF DIESEL GENERATORS

The title of Section 2 of the Bill, 8113.15, should be amended to read: “Provision of 40MW of Temporary Power and Maintenance, Operation, and Overhaul of Diesel Generators.” §8113.15 would be amended to read: “…the Guam Power Authority (“GPA”) with all deliberate speed, and with the consent with of the Guam Public Utilities Commission (“GPUC”) shall proceed with the procurement for a vendor or vendors to provide 40MW of Temporary Power, and to maintain, operate, and overhaul diesel generators…”.

## THE PUC IS WILLING AND CAPABLE OF UNDERTAKING THE PROCURMENT REVIEW FUNCTIONS IMPOSED UPON IT BY THIS BILL

Essentially, this Bill would place responsibility upon the PUC for reviewing procurements by GPA made under the special provisions of Bill 201-37 (COR). The PUC is not technically a procurement body. Its core function is utility regulation and rate setting. However, under its existing Contract Review Protocol with GPA, the PUC currently does review all proposed procurements of GPA in excess of $1.5M. Ordinarily, PUC reviews GPA procurements to assure basic compliance with procurement laws. The PUC has Commissioners, Administrative Law Judges, and the PUC Counsel who are familiar with procurement laws and well versed in their application. The PUC would seek to assure that the procurement procedures used by GPA for procurement under this Bill would be done in a fair and objective manner.

## CONCLUSION

The adoption of Bill No. 201-37(COR) should assist GPA in implementing solutions to reduce the occurrence of load shedding. The Guam Legislature should fully support this Bill and advocate its enactment into law.

---

Thank you for your consideration of this Testimony.

Sincerely,

Jeffrey C. Johnson
Chairman

Subject: Request to Confirm Substantial Interest Declaration, OPA-PA-23-004

Dear Attorney General,

The attached GPA filing to the Office of the Public Auditor is transmitted herewith for your review and
confirmation, pursuant to 5 G.C.A. §5425(g)(1).

All oppositions to this filing are due by Friday, November 17, 2023 by 5 p.m. so I ask for your support and 
signature on the attached indicating that you **CONCUR** with GPA’s determination of substantial interests by 
Wednesday, November 15, 2023 so we may timely file your concurrence with the OPA.

This request is being made in compliance with the laws of Guam which require a written determination from the 
head of the purchasing agency and concurrence from the Attorney General to lift the stay on the above-referenced 
procurement permitting GPA to increase generation capacity and allow GPA to concurrently meet customer loads 
as well as provide necessary reserve to support emergency maintenance and outages at our aging plants 
minimizing or avoiding load shedding.

I can be reached at 671-648-3180 or by email at <u>jbenavente@gpagwa.com</u>, should you need clarification or have
